chunks: When God said: "O Jesus, I will take you to Myself and exalt you, and rid you of the infidels, and hold those who follow you above those who disbelieve till the Day of Resurrection. You have then to come back to Me when I will judge between you in what you were at variance."
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about Jesus's death, ascension, and the fate of his followers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'tawaffa' is often interpreted as taking the soul in a state of sleep or death prior to ascension, distinguishing it from the final death at the end of time. This verse underscores the unique status of Jesus (peace be upon him) as a purified prophet whose followers will remain superior to disbelievers until the Day of Judgment, where God will arbitrate their theological differences. It serves as a foundational text for the belief in Jesus' physical ascension and his eventual return (in some traditions) or final reckoning.
